The jury has the final word whether the person is innocent or guilty. Jury nullification is when the jury believes the person guilty, but they say innocent instead.

Say you have a guy accused of possessing and using marijuana. They found a crap ton of marijuana in his house and car, have videos of him smoking it in public, and tested positive multiple time. There's no denying the guy is a stoner. However, the jury says "innocent" because they don't agree with the marijuana laws.

If you know that a law like possession of Marijuana is bull shit. You can vote not-guilty despite the fact that it is illegal to possess Marijuana.

I love how almost every conversation on Jury Nullification has people mentioning marijuana, but we still don't see it happening in trails. The prosecution convinces too many people that are arrested to just plead out for a lesser sentence. We need to start convincing people to stand trial so these conversations can actually play out.

The risks is too high in must cases. They slammed tou with every charge possible and due to minimum sentencing laws you are usually looking at a long prison sentence. Or a plea deal for only one of the lessor charges. Things like 15 years in jail verus 30 days.

The issue is that, usually, when you are put on a jury, a lawyer asks if you have any convictions that will prevent you from strictly adhering to what the law says. If you lie and say no, but then vote based on a conviction, that's perjury and it's illegal. A felony. With up to 5 years in prison.

The easy solution to that is to vote and never use your convictions as the reason for why. But it's not so easy because people are gonna ask why. It's also not easy, because if they don't know that you are doing it because "Smoking marijuana shouldn't be illegal", it won't matter.

In ancient times, there was a primordial sea that was thick with green goo and slop. Late one evening, as one accursed creature pursued another deep underwater with ill intentions, the surface between to quicken. Soon these tiny vibrations ripened into enormous sloshing waves.

There was an explosion that killed much of the life in the ocean, and a pillar of fire and mist rose from the sea, and the Great Volcano (as it was later called, never being given any other name) emerged like a mountain of red hot iron.

Slowly the volcano cooled, and its eruptions became less frequent, and a web-like plant that would eventually be called Narl Weed began to grow on its jagged shores.

Following the last eruption of the Great Volcano, two large and powerful but exhausted metallic creatures crawled out of the cone. These were the first Holnareem to emerge from beneath the surface.

Prior to this, they had existed in a semi-conscious state, feeding directly from the molten magma deep under the world's crust. But as they rose in the open air under the bright stars, they became more aware of themselves and each other. They started to argue, and soon after the first battle of the Holnareem began. But it didn't last long, as there was little to fight about, with plenty of minerals to eat and much space to explore. They soon agreed upon the first words of their language (which has long since been lost).

In a short time (a few decades in human terms), several more Holnareem emerged from inside the nearly dormant volcanic crater. These newcomers still remembered something of their creation, although their memories were veiled in deep darkness. Soon they forgot everything about the creator and the circumstances of their inception. And they felt little curiosity, as they lived in great joy on the volcanic Island of the Holnareem.

At least, their lives were dominated by joy. But there was some tension among them, as the Narl Weed grew much more thickly and vibrantly on the side of the island facing the direction of the rising of the sun at dawn. The largest and most powerful among them usually got first pick of the best plants which would rise in the morning (this being an extremely fast-growing species). But most of the time, even the weakest among them did get a share, and none ever went hungry.

One generation passed, then another. As time progressed, the Holnareem began to become disillusioned, realizing that they were not all equal.

A single Holnareem among them in particular came to establish himself as the first among equals. It was he who first chose an individual name for himself: Tlakorr the Strong. When disputes would arise concerning whose turn it was to eat the freshest, most desirable Narl Weed (the tastiest had a slight purplish tinge at the heart of their webs), they began to turn to Tlakorr, who was considered to be not only the strongest, but the most wise. His decisions were so wise and just that nobody objected when he began issuing himself an extra portion of the finest weeds during each lunar cycle. And minerals were still so plentiful on the island that no one even noticed that the choicest stones and gems always went down Tlakorr's throat.

This social structure might have endured forever, if it weren't for the new art of body engraving, and the Holnareem who invented it, who was the second to create his own name: Tallwaaz the Absent.
